title: Being a Good Neighbor
short: Greet neighbors, keep noise, pets and yard tidy, park considerately, warn them about a party or project, and talk to them directly about a problem.
trouble: Learners complain to a landlord or online before a friendly word. A direct, friendly conversation solves most problems.

blocks.html: Neighbors are people you borrow and lend with, wave to every morning and share walls, fences and streets with. Small courtesies make years of living side by side pleasant.
Greet neighbors. Keep noise, pets and yard tidy. Park considerately. Warn them about a party or a big project. Talk to them directly, and kindly, about a problem.

Your home is next to theirs, so your sounds, pets, cars and yard become part of their home too. A friendly hello builds goodwill for the day you need a favor or have to raise a concern. A heads-up about a party or a roofing job lets them plan. When something bothers you, a direct, friendly word gives them a chance to fix it, while going to a landlord or posting online first turns a small issue into a feud.

say: Hi, Mr. Diaz! Just a heads-up: we're having a few friends over Saturday evening. If it gets loud, please let me know.
Thanks for telling me, Kofi. Have fun!
opts.narr: A heads-up goes a long way.

blocks.title: A barking dog
blocks.q: Rosa's neighbor's dog barks for hours each day while the neighbor is at work. What should she do first?
steps: The neighbor may not know, since it happens while they are away.
Rosa knocks or leaves a friendly note: "Hi! I wanted to let you know that Max barks a lot during the day. I thought you'd want to know."
Only if that doesn't help would she go to the landlord or an association.
blocks.a: Talk to the neighbor directly and kindly first.

blocks.title: A big project
blocks.q: James is having his roof replaced next week. What would a good neighbor do?
steps: Tell the neighbors ahead about the dates and the noise.
Ask the crew to keep trucks clear of driveways.
Thank the neighbors for their patience afterward.
